period: start of 2025 (BPE reference date), not a tax year
method: Figures were read from the downloaded workbook on the access date by tools/extract_uk_firm_bpe_tables.py; none was filled from memory. Numbers are the cells as published: business counts in businesses, employment, employees and working proprietors in thousands of people, turnover in millions of pounds. A cell published as [c] (disclosive) is left empty and flagged [c]. Band labels lose their [Note n] markers; percentage columns are not kept.

source.edition: BUSINESS POPULATION ESTIMATES FOR THE UK AND REGIONS 2025; Published 2nd October 2025

tables.Table 1: Number and percentage of businesses in the private sector and their associated employment and turnover, by number of employees, UK, start 2025
tables.Table 2: Number and percentage of businesses and other organisations in the whole economy, private sector, central and local government, and non-profit organisations with associated employment and turnover, start 2025
tables.Table 3: Number and percentage of businesses in the private sector and associated employment and turnover, by legal status and number of employees, UK, start 2025

notes: Employment is employees plus working proprietors (Table 1 note 3). Companies with one PAYE employee on the IDBR are counted with no employees, the employee being treated as a working proprietor (Table 3 notes 3 and 6). Businesses with no employees are registered (VAT and/or PAYE) or unregistered (Table 3 note 2). Companies include public corporations and nationalised bodies (Table 3 heading). Turnover excludes SIC 2007 Section K. Business counts are rounded, so totals may not equal the sum of their parts.
